title: SK Hynix Shares Rise as OpenAI Negotiates for More Memory Chips in South Korea

tickers.name: SK hynix Inc. American Depositary Shares

summary:
The shortage of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) has become a binding constraint for artificial intelligence buildouts, prompting OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to meet with leaders at Samsung and SK Hynix in South Korea to secure additional capacity. Shares of SK Hynix climbed 2.4% on reports of the visit and subsequent talks regarding HBM supply for OpenAI's Stargate infrastructure project. The semiconductor maker noted that customer requests for its HBM products currently exceed its available supply by more than twofold.

During his trip, Altman met with about 50 Samsung executives in Yongin to discuss the role of AI in business over the next decade and the scaling of data centers. The meetings build on letters of intent signed in October 2025, under which the two chipmakers targeted the combined delivery of as many as 900,000 DRAM wafers a month. The pursuit of these components comes as Altman recently criticized the allocation of scarce memory to personal computers, arguing the chips are underutilized compared to their use in AI data centers.

SK HYNIX JUMPS 2.4% AFTER OPENAI CEO'S SOUTH KOREA VISIT

SK hynix shares rose 2.4% after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman reportedly met SK Group executives to discuss HBM supply and Stargate AI infrastructure.

SK hynix says customers are requesting more than twice its available HBM supply.

Nomura remains bullish, while Rosenblatt reiterated its Buy rating, dismissing recent competitive concerns.

Reports also suggest a potential $12 billion special dividend linked to Kioxia investment gains.

selectedTweets.text:
According to Korean media, Sam Altman met about 50 Samsung executives in Yongin on Saturday.

It was his first visit to Korea since October of last year, when OpenAI signed letters of intent with Samsung and SK Hynix for up to 900,000 DRAM wafers per month.

On the same day, he had lunch with SK chairman Chey Tae-won, who brought executives from SK Hynix and SK Telecom. HBM supply and data centers were reportedly on the table.

This comes just days after Altman said it is "quite terrible" for scarce DRAM to sit inside personal computers.

The biggest AI customer in the world flew to Korea to talk to the two companies that make the memory and that tells you exactly where the bottleneck is.

Sam Altman just said it is "quite terrible" for your PC to have RAM.

His point is that the memory in a home computer sits idle about 95% of the time, while the same chips in a data center would be working almost all day.

That is a remarkable thing for the CEO of OpenAI to say out loud in the middle of a memory shortage.

It tells you where the AI labs want every DRAM chip to go, and it is NOT your laptop.

selectedTweets.text:
Bloomberg: Sam Altman met about 50 Samsung executives in South Korea, seeking deeper memory-chip and data-center ties as shortages bite.

Memory has become a binding constraint on AI buildouts, with shortages across many memory products pushing chip prices sharply higher.

South Korea leads in advanced memory, so Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and AMD’s Lisa Su have each visited twice since last year.

Saturday’s talks extend an earlier deal under which Samsung supplies memory for OpenAI’s Stargate project and works with OpenAI on data centers, including floating offshore sites.

When that deal was signed in October 2025, OpenAI said Samsung and SK Hynix were targeting up to 900K DRAM wafers a month combined.
